## Highlights since 0.16.10

- **Much lower idle CPU and energy use.** The Agent panel no longer runs a hidden per-frame loop. It caused about 90% of Lattice's idle CPU use and most of its background wakeups, even when the panel was hidden.
- **Agent tasks use a provider you have connected.** Proofreading, polishing, compile repair and Git commit messages use whichever AI provider you have connected, right after launch. Claude-only setups no longer see "Codex CLI is required".
- **Continue in terminal.** The Agent can copy a command that continues the current chat in Codex CLI or Claude Code.

## Notable fixes

- Each compiled document keeps its own PDF tab. Thanks to @surajinacademia.
- Markdown comments use a lighter highlight, and the comment box closes when you click outside it or press Escape, keeping your text.
- Commenting works right after the Agent edits a file in an Overleaf-linked project.
- The error panel names the undefined command for documents in subfolders, says when the error list is capped, and says when an automatic repair left errors.
- When a newer version of Lattice may already fix a failure, Lattice tells you and offers an Update button.
- The outline no longer covers the search panel's close button. Thanks to @BrianCyan.
- On Windows, Ctrl+wheel PDF zoom is gentler and middle-click autoscroll works. Thanks to @LucasDavidTPE.
- Fixes to the Windows development setup. Thanks to @skytheacademic.
